children: U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche on Tuesday pushed back against suggestions that Nvidia or Huang is under criminal investigation, while refusing to provide any further details related to the chipmaker.

"Nvidia is a good corporate citizen," Blanche told reporters while speaking at a Justice Department press conference on Tuesday. "Obviously, if Nvidia was the target, or was subject to some criminal investigation, or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people."

Pressed on what the Justice Department had investigated regarding Huang and what conclusions were reached, Blanche declined to reveal private discussions with President Donald Trump, noting the president spoke with many people before encouraging the board to restore Huang.

FBI Director Kash Patel, appearing alongside Blanche, also declined to say whether investigators had spoken with Huang or whether the bureau knew of intelligence assessments involving Alice Huang, a woman U.S. officials suspected of being an intelligence asset for Beijing.

Jensen Huang stepped down less than two weeks before his Monday comeback. Reports surrounding his exit pointed to alleged relationships with two Nvidia employees and heightened national security questions tied to Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore firm that buys Nvidia semiconductors. Alice Huang was also alleged to be a Chinese intelligence spy.

In mid-November, the Justice and Commerce departments announced an inquiry into Megaspeed over potential violations of U.S. export controls involving Nvidia chips routed toward China. Blanche had previously said on Nov. 12 that federal prosecutors had not reached conclusions about Alice Huang's background, and on Tuesday he said the department regularly conducts hundreds or more export investigations at a time when asked about ongoing export scrutiny. China has denied trying to spy on the Nvidia chief.

Speaking to CNBC on Monday, Trump voiced strong backing for Huang's return, remarking that an extensive evaluation indicated the executive demonstrated questionable judgment in separate matters instead of engaging in criminal misconduct. Additionally, Trump shared on social media that Blanche affirmed law enforcement possessed no proof of illegal actions by Huang, while the board of Nvidia noted it consulted top U.S. officials to confirm his reinstatement presented no risk to national security.

The news of Huang's reinstatement sent Nvidia's stock surging 31% on Monday, though shares gave back ground on Tuesday as investors continue to fret about ongoing federal investigations along with one by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was trending in ‘neutral’ territory on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), ‘bearish’ on the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA) and ‘bullish’ on the tech-heavy Invesco QQQ (QQQ).
Attorney General Todd Blanche praised Nvidia as "a good corporate citizen" and said the company is not facing criminal scrutiny.
Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel avoided answering direct questions about any investigation tied to Jensen Huang's reinstatement, in a recent press conference.
Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO on Monday, which sparked a sharp stock rally before shares pulled back Tuesday.

title: US Attorney General Praises Nvidia As Questions Swirl Over Huang’s Reinstatement
